study: Boylan et al. (2018), ScratchMaths efficacy trial (UCL programme, EEF/Sheffield Hallam evaluation)
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned independent evaluation by Sheffield Hallam University; the programme was developed by a separate party (UCL Knowledge Lab / UCL Institute of Education). Evaluators are not the developers.
developer_evidence: 'ScratchMaths was developed and delivered by the UCL Knowledge Lab'; report notes 'the intervention worked under developer-led conditions.' The developing team ran the PD.
cascade_evidence: Developer-led PD delivered directly to participating teachers at central hub events (2.5 PD days/yr in 7 geographical hubs); no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher tier - UCL ran the PD for the teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: Two-arm trial with business-as-usual / wait-list control (control schools continued normal maths/computing; Year-2 waitlist crossover only after the primary outcome). No active alternative PD given to control during the contrast.
coaching_evidence: PD was centralised hub workshops (two PD days/yr plus optional follow-up half-days), engaging teachers in the activities; no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers in their own classrooms reported.
student_dose_evidence: ScratchMaths is a teacher-delivered computing+maths curriculum taught during normal class time; pupils do Scratch activities as part of the regular lesson, not as an added tutoring/pull-out or independent software dose beyond instruction.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes from the programme's first (and only) rollout, with teachers new to ScratchMaths; KS2 measured at the end of the 2-year programme. Multi-year-by-design (so not single_year_design), but teachers were in their first experience delivering it.
